abstract: This study investigates how anthropomorphic perceptions of AI service robots influence consumer adoption choice, emphasizing the mediating role of technology attachment and the moderating role of robot use self-efficacy. Data were collected from 380 U.S. participants via an online survey panel. Participants evaluated anthropomorphism, robot use self-efficacy, technology attachment, likelihood of AI usage, and decisions about AI behavioral adoption choice. Using a moderated mediation model, the findings reveal that anthropomorphism increases the likelihood of AI usage and AI behavioral adoption choice both directly and indirectly through technology attachment. The indirect effect depends on self-efficacy—when consumers report higher robot use self-efficacy, anthropomorphism strongly predicts technology attachment, which enhances AI usage likelihood and AI behavioral adoption choice; at low self-efficacy, this relationship weakens. These results extend Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) paradigm and self-efficacy theory by illustrating the psychological mechanisms underlying consumer responses to AI in services. Practically, anthropomorphic AI design should be paired with efforts to enhance user self-efficacy, such as tutorials, guided trials, and support. Overall, this research integrates anthropomorphism, attachment, and self-efficacy into a unified framework explaining consumer adoption of AI service robots, contributing both theoretical depth and actionable managerial insights.

ur.tldr: 探究拟人化感知如何影响消费者对AI服务机器人的采纳。基于380名美国在线问卷数据，构建有调节的中介模型，发现拟人化既直接又通过技术依恋间接提升AI使用可能性与行为采纳意愿；机器人使用自我效能感起调节作用——高自我效能下拟人化对技术依恋的预测更强，低自我效能下关系减弱。扩展了CASA范式与自我效能理论，建议设计拟人化AI时搭配教程与引导试用以提升用户自我效能。

title: Making Robots Relatable: The Role of Self-Efficacy in AI Adoption
title_zh: 让机器人更具亲和力：自我效能感在AI采纳中的作用
